samples.text:
The chart shows why adults in three age groups take part-time courses in the evening at a college.

For the under 30 group, the main reason is career progression with 42%. Change of career is 26% and personal interest is 15%. Only 12% say their employer require it and 5% want to meet people.

The 30–50 group is quite similar to the younger group. Career progression is 30% and change of career is 28%, so they are nearly the same. Personal interest is 20% and required by employer is 18%, which is the highest for this reason. Meet people is the lowest at 4%.

However, the over 50 group is very different. More than half of them, 55%, study because of personal interest. Also, 20% of them want to meet people, which is much higher than the other groups. Career reasons is less important for them, change of career is 12%, career progression is 8% and required by employer is only 5%.

Overall, younger learners mostly study for their job, but older learners study for interest.
samples.why: Figures accurate and all groups covered · short, basic overview at the end · mechanical, repetitive sentence patterns · limited vocabulary · agreement and punctuation errors that do not impede meaning.

samples.text:
The bar chart compares the main motivations of three age groups of adults for enrolling in part-time evening courses at a college.

Overall, learners under 50 were mainly motivated by work-related reasons, whereas those over 50 studied primarily out of personal interest. Meeting people was a relatively unimportant reason for all groups except the oldest.

Career progression was the most common reason among learners under 30, cited by 42%, and it was also the top reason for the 30–50 group, although at a lower 30%. For both of these groups, changing career was the second most important factor, at 26% and 28% respectively. Being required by an employer was mentioned by 12% of the youngest learners and 18% of the middle group, while personal interest accounted for 15% and 20%.

The pattern for over-50s was completely different. More than half of this group (55%) took courses for personal interest, and a further 20% wanted to meet people, which was four times the figure for under-30s and five times that for the 30–50 group. By contrast, only 8% of older learners wanted to progress in their careers, 12% hoped to change career and just 5% were required to study by their employer.
samples.why: Clear overview contrasting work-related and personal motives · key features highlighted and compared across groups · good cohesion · some less common vocabulary · generally accurate with a minor slip.

samples.text:
The chart illustrates the reasons adults in three age brackets gave for attending part-time evening courses at a college.

A clear generational divide is evident. For learners under 50, the main motivations were professional, with career progression and career change dominating, whereas the over-50s were driven predominantly by personal interest and, to a lesser extent, the opportunity to socialise.

Among those under 30, career progression was by far the leading reason, given by 42%, followed by a change of career (26%). The 30–50 age group showed a similar but more evenly balanced profile: career progression (30%) and career change (28%) were almost equally important, and this group was also the most likely to be studying at an employer's request (18%). Personal interest was a secondary motive for both groups, at 15% and 20%, and very few learners in either group mentioned meeting people.

For the over-50s, the picture was reversed. Personal interest accounted for 55% of responses, more than the three work-related reasons combined, and 20% saw the courses as a way to meet people. Career-related reasons, meanwhile, were marginal: only 8% cited career progression, 12% a change of career and 5% an employer requirement.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected around a clear generational contrast · well-placed overview · selective, accurate figures · sophisticated cohesion · wide, precise vocabulary · varied complex structures without error.
